title: Frontend: Rate Limiter
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Rate Limiter. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Implement solution({capacity,refillPerSecond,events}). Start full at time 0. Each event {time,cost} uses nondecreasing milliseconds and nonnegative cost. Refill continuously, cap at capacity, consume only when affordable; return accepted booleans. This is one deterministic token bucket, not shared-server coordination.
constraints: Define solution(input) in plain JavaScript. Return the documented JSON-compatible value or throw the documented validation error. Each case receives a fresh input.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Keep capacity, refill rate, current tokens, and the last update instant.
alternativeApproaches: Design an atomic shared-store update for multiple servers and state how fail-open versus fail-closed affects the product.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Initial burst; exact boundary; partial refill.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
